title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent; that same candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition that was run. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7...00ede; immutable master-prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e...15ba).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), offering potential to reduce human effort in authoring device CLI sequences. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior surveys and empirical work document LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A common architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. These pipelines reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, ordering, simple policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

Research question and contribution. We ask: when the same natural-language intent is realized by a single LLM-generated configuration candidate and that identical candidate is (a) accepted as-is (baseline) or (b) submitted to a deterministic validator plus up to one automated repair (guarded), what is the paired difference in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction on a synthetic/emulation partition? Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (shared_initial_candidate semantics) that quantifies the marginal verifier+single-repair effect on identical candidates for N_pairs = 250 intents, reports exact reconciliation counts and inferential bounds, and archives full validator traces and execution manifests for auditability.
sections.related_work: Existing surveys and empirical studies motivate GVR architectures and verification-based pipelines for LLM-assisted configuration. NetConfEval and related NetOps evaluations demonstrate that LLMs can produce useful draft configurations in controlled settings but still require verification layers for safe deployment [1],[2]. Verified prompt programming and workflow papers show how localized verifier feedback can drive automatic correction and improve verified outcomes in configuration and code domains [3],[4]. Tool and verifier evolution (for example Batfish and header-space/model-checking approaches) provide mature mechanized checks for forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [5]. Security analyses of indirect and direct prompt-injection emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines [6]. Our study differs from prior work by using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the marginal effect of deterministic validation and a single bounded repair on identical generated candidates, and by publishing deterministic reconciliation and provider-call accounting for stage-level auditing.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion rules, analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the model-call budget (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7...00ede). The preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the executed confirmatory analysis applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider accounting. Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that same generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded); no independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. Provider-call reconciliation reports model_calls_used = 251, decomposed into 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair-stage call (stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}). These stage-level counts are reported in the archived deterministic reconciliation artifact and were used in the numeric accounting presented below.

Task bank and validator. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard/extreme). The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, checking required_sequence ordering, enforcing workflow constraints (group-activity and make-before-break rules), and comparing the resulting final_state snapshot to the task's expected_final_state. When the validator returned valid = false for a guarded episode, the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair (syntactic/order fixes only) and re-submitted the repaired candidate once; no multi-iteration repair or human escalation was performed by design.

Inclusion and missingness rules. Preregistered exclusions removed items that prevented deterministic verification (vendor-parser fatal errors) or contained denylist/credential-like tokens. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items would be excluded from the primary analysis and handled in sensitivity treatments. In this executed confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged and complete_pair_count = 250.

Analysis. The primary analysis used an exact two-sided McNemar test on paired binary validator outcomes and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All analysis inputs and outputs are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.results:
Execution and raw counts. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair-stage call (stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}).

Primary outcomes and contingency. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on the discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numeric outputs and bootstrap parameters are archived in the analysis artifacts.

Representative validator diagnostics and repairs. Validator traces for passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count for the task payloads' required_sequence; representative examples (hard-difficulty tasks) appear in the archived scoring artifacts. Only one automated repair was exercised; its trace and the corresponding guarded-pass scoring record are archived and reconcile to the single repair-stage model call recorded above.

Missingness and exclusions. No episodes were excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis: complete_pairs = 250 and all missingness counts = 0. Contamination detectors flagged no confirmatory episodes, so no preregistered sensitivity exclusion was required for the confirmatory estimand.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the near-null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the lone failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the maximum verifier-detected improvement under this pipeline and task scope.

Why the observed gain is small. Artifact-grounded explanations include: (1) the task generator encoded constrained intents, allowed_touched_fields, and explicit required_sequences that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences under these constraints; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, required ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) and does not capture broader semantic or live-protocol correctness.

Power and assumption note. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 to detect a 15 pp absolute effect with N = 250. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and reduces the ability to detect small absolute improvements; therefore the paired-bootstrap CI (reported above) is the most practically informative summary for small-effect magnitudes.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but not live protocol dynamics. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; the preregistered community and production-like partitions and the preregistered sim-to-real contrast were not executed and remain untested in this run. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised. These limitations constrain how broadly the numeric bounds should be generalized.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, gpt-5-mini initial candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is restricted to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development and rehearsal only.

Models, tools, and execution accounting: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded in the execution manifest); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Confirmatory execution completed 500 episodes (250 paired intents) with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation calls + 1 repair-stage call) and stage_counts summarized as {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} as reconciled in the archived deterministic reconciliation artifact. Complete_pair_count = 250; baseline_success_count = 249; guarded_success_count = 250; contingency counts n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Preregistration and immutable prompt references: preregistration id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7...00ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1...15ba). The evidence bundle archives the full execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript; the preregistration and master-prompt SHA-256 values above provide concise immutable anchors into that archive.

Executed estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration specified multiple partitions including a sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported in this paper is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics). No manual manuscript editing of technical content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions and the sim-to-real confirmatory contrast were not executed.
Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) but did not measure broader semantic or live-protocol correctness.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adaptive adversaries and retrieval-based prompt-injection attacks were not exercised and remain open operational threats.
